title: Remove All Nodes With a Value

concept.title: The head can be removed too
body: To delete a node you need the node **before** it. That is a problem for the head: nothing stands before it, and removing the head changes which node is the head. Many list algorithms avoid this special case with a **dummy node** placed in front of the real head. After the work, the answer is `dummy.next`.
The loop looks one node ahead of `cur` (`cur.next`), which is exactly the node to be deleted. When the whole list is removed, `dummy.next` becomes `None` and the output is `empty`.

statement: Remove all nodes of a singly linked list whose value equals `val`, and print the remaining list. If no node remains, print `empty`.
inputFormat: The second line has the values of the nodes, from the head to the tail.
outputFormat: Print the remaining values on one line, or `empty`.
hints: Put a dummy node in front of the head, so that the head can be removed like any other node.
Look at `cur.next`: if its value is the target, set `cur.next = cur.next.next`.
Move `cur` forward only when you did not delete.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

# Every node is also remembered in this list. Python in the browser cannot free a very long chain of nodes at once,
# so free_nodes() (called at the end) cuts the links first and the nodes are then freed one by one.
all_nodes = []


class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        all_nodes.append(self)


def free_nodes():
    for node in all_nodes:
        node.next = None
        if hasattr(node, "random"):
            node.random = None
    all_nodes.clear()


# Builds a list from the values. If pos is 0 or more, the last node points back to the node at index pos (a cycle).
def build_list(values, pos=-1):
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = ListNode(v, head)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        for _ in range(pos):
            target = target.next
        tail.next = target
    return head


# Prints the values of a list on one line ("empty" for an empty list).
def print_list(head):
    out = []
    while head is not None:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    print(*(out if out else ["empty"]))

n, val = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

print_list(remove_elements(build_list(a), val))

explanation: A dummy node in front of the head lets the head be deleted like any other node. `cur.next` is the candidate for deletion; `cur` only advances when nothing was deleted.
